scope: Replacement of unsupported RLIMIT_AS with host-observed per-process resident-memory enforcement; no scientific checker was invoked.

findings: Every supervised command starts a new session, making its PID the process-group identifier used for observation and termination.
The monitor reads every process group's resident set through the host /bin/ps interface every 10 milliseconds and compares each process independently to the supplied ceiling.
The first observed per-process breach kills the complete process group; observation failure also kills the group and is classified as an infrastructure/audit failure.
Receipts retain enforcement method, sample count, maximum observed per-process RSS, breach status, observation error, /usr/bin/time metrics, and process-group cleanup evidence.
The regression holds a 128 MiB allocation against a 64 MiB test ceiling, requires observed breach and cleanup, and separately retains the frozen 2 GiB value in execution-manifest validation.
runner.claim_limit: This is sampled resident-memory enforcement, not a hard virtual-address-space limit; it stops a process group at the first host-observed breach and does not claim zero transient overshoot between 10 ms samples.
